crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices and the assignment of general ledger codes, cost centres and tax treatments before payment runs. It spans scanned paper, PDF attachments, emailed invoices and structured e-invoice feeds, and it ends where the approved invoice posts to the ledger. The work sits inside accounts payable but touches procurement, tax and master data, because a wrong vendor record or tax code breaks the coding downstream.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Most stacks combine optical character recognition or document AI for text extraction with a matching engine that checks the invoice against purchase orders and goods receipts. Capture tools read the header fields, line items, totals and tax breakdowns, then a rules layer or a learned model proposes the coding. The system usually sits between an email or supplier portal intake channel and an ERP such as SAP, Oracle or NetSuite, with a queue for exceptions that a human reviews.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The common pattern is three way matching: invoice, purchase order and receipt must agree within tolerance before the invoice is cleared for payment. Where no purchase order exists, coding falls back to vendor history, prior invoices and keyword rules, and increasingly to a language model that reads the line description and suggests an account. Confidence scores route clean invoices straight through and send the rest to a clerk, who corrects the code and, in a well run setup, that correction feeds back as training data.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The audit trail matters more than the extraction accuracy, because tax authorities and external auditors want to see who approved what and on what evidence. Invoice data carries bank details, so fraud controls against changed remittance accounts are a standard part of the process, and duplicate detection guards against paying the same invoice twice. Retention rules, VAT and sales tax documentation requirements, and access controls over who can alter a vendor record all sit in this layer, and any model that proposes a code should be explainable enough to defend in a review.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward fewer human touches on clean invoices and more effort spent on exceptions, supplier onboarding and fraud detection. Mandated e-invoicing regimes are shifting capture from reading documents to receiving structured data, which changes the skill mix from OCR tuning to data mapping and controls. The open questions are how much coding a model should be allowed to commit without review, and how teams evidence that a learned coding decision was correct when an auditor asks.
